findings.evidence: Write the message in Conventional Commits 1.0.0: `type(scope)!: subject`, a blank line, a body saying why, then footers
findings.fix: Shorten to 'Conventional Commits 1.0.0; `!` or `BREAKING CHANGE:` only for a real compatibility break'. The model already knows the header/body/footer layout, and the spec edge cases are already in references/commit-message-template.md.

findings.evidence: 2. Plan each commit as paths, plus hunks for a mixed file.
findings.fix: Add a short decision rule for commit boundaries that are hard to call, e.g. 'Before splitting, ask: does each commit build and pass tests alone? A rename plus edits, or a refactor that the feature depends on, goes first as its own commit; when one hunk serves both, keep them together and say so.'

findings.evidence: Gotchas cover in-progress operations, GIT_INDEX_FILE in fresh shells, `--only` and `git stash`, but not the other ways `git commit` blocks in an agent shell
findings.fix: Add a gotcha: 'With `commit.gpgsign` set, `git commit` can block on a pinentry or passphrase prompt that an agent shell cannot answer. When the commit hangs or fails with a signing error, report it and ask; never add `--no-gpg-sign` unprompted, because the repository may require signed commits.'

findings.evidence: Use when asked to commit, check in or save work to git, stage selected files or hunks, split a mixed tree into commits, review what is staged, or draft a commit message.
findings.fix: Stage and commit Git changes so each commit holds only the approved change, leaving content the user already staged untouched, splitting mixed hunks without an interactive terminal, verifying the staged version rather than the working tree, and writing Conventional Commits messages that pass commitlint. Use when asked to commit, check in, wrap up or save work to git, stage selected files or hunks, split uncommitted changes into logical commits, review what is staged before a push, or draft a commit message, even if the user never says 'commit' or 'git add'. Not for rebasing, squashing, amending or force-pushing history, splitting existing commits, resolving merge conflicts, opening pull requests, or code review unrelated to a commit.

findings.evidence: The 8 evals cover draft-message and commit, but none covers the 'review what is staged' or 'stage changes' routes, or a repository with commitlint rules that should load references/commit-message-template.md
findings.fix: Add three evals with fixtures: (1) 'stage only the auth changes, I'll commit myself' with user-staged content, asserting no `git commit` and the user's entries untouched; (2) 'check what I've staged' with a staged .env or lockfile churn, asserting it is flagged and the index is not changed; (3) a repo with commitlint.config.js extending config-conventional, asserting a lower-case subject and an allowed type.

findings.evidence: | draft a message | step 1, then give the message text only | propose or run any git command, `git commit -F` included |
findings.fix: Resolve the contradiction: step 1 runs `git status`, `git diff --cached` and `git diff`, but the Never column forbids running any git command. Change the Never cell to 'run or propose any command that changes the index, the tree or history (`git add`, `git reset`, `git commit`, `git commit -F` included); read-only step 1 commands are allowed'.

Add fallbacks for the branches that fail here. On an unborn branch (no HEAD), `git read-tree HEAD` fails, so use `git read-tree --empty` instead. In step 5, put the checkout-index target outside the worktree (e.g. `<gitdir>/commit-work-verify/`) so the export does not show up as untracked files.

findings.evidence: 'A commit is one change that builds and tests on its own' and 'Plan each commit as paths, plus hunks for a mixed file' repeat familiar commit-helper guidance. By section line count, the 11-line intent router is chiefly activation, the 15-line Workflow is mostly expert with some generic reminders, and the six-line Gotchas is expert; activation therefore occupies substantially more than the rubric's preferred share.
findings.fix: Remove the generic opening definition and standalone planning reminder, and compress ordinary message/review/stage routing while preserving its safety constraints. Retain the distinctive temporary-index, non-interactive patch, staged-version verification and hook-handling procedures.

findings.evidence: The message-only route requires 'step 1' but forbids 'propose or run any git command'. Step 1 requires reading 'git status', 'git diff --cached' and 'git diff'. For a request to draft a message from the current index without supplied command output, these instructions cannot both be followed.
findings.fix: Give message-only requests a separate inspection rule: use a supplied staged diff without commands; otherwise permit read-only Git inspection. Keep the final response message-only and forbid index/worktree mutation and commit commands. Adjust the message-only eval assertion to allow read-only inspection when no diff was supplied.

findings.evidence: Stage-only requests must use 'the real index; leave the user's entries in it alone', but step 4 requires the exact index to contain 'only the approved change'. Staging an approved auth change while preserving an unrelated, already-staged configuration change cannot satisfy that whole-index invariant.
findings.fix: Make the invariant intent-specific: for a commit, the commit index must contain only approved changes; for stage-only work, review the newly staged delta, verify that pre-existing staged entries remain unchanged, and explicitly report those retained entries.

findings.evidence: The temporary-index branch always starts with 'GIT_INDEX_FILE=<gitdir>/commit-work.index git read-tree HEAD'. In a repository without its first commit, a request to commit selected work while leaving unrelated staged content untouched reaches this branch, but HEAD does not exist and the prescribed initialization fails.
findings.fix: Before initializing the temporary index, check whether HEAD resolves to a commit. Use the prescribed read-tree HEAD initialization when it does; otherwise initialize the temporary index with git read-tree --empty, retaining the same explicit GIT_INDEX_FILE prefix throughout the workflow.
